sanskrit: puṇyapāpaviyuktānāṃ sthānam āhur manīṣiṇām śāsvataṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva akṣaraṃ cābhayaṃ ca yat
english: The wise declare that, for those freed from both merit and demerit, there is an abode that is everlasting, imperishable, indestructible, and without fear.

sanskrit: jñānināṃ saṃbhavaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sthānam avraṇam acyutam atīndriyam abījaṃ ca janmamṛtyutamonudam
english: It is the highest origin of the knowers — a station flawless and unfailing, beyond the senses, without seed, the dispeller of birth, death, and darkness.

sanskrit: avyaktasthaṃ paraṃ yat tat pṛṣṭas te 'haṃ narādhipa sa eṣa prakṛtiṣṭho hi tasthur ity abhidhīyate
english: That supreme thing seated in the Unmanifest, about which you have questioned me, O lord of men — this very one, abiding in primordial Nature, is called the Stationary.

sanskrit: acetanaś caiṣa mataḥ prakṛtisthaś ca pārthiva etenādhiṣṭhitaś caiva sṛjate saṃharaty api
english: And this one, O king, is held to be without consciousness and seated in Nature; yet, presided over by the conscious Self, it both creates and withdraws the world.

sanskrit: janaka uvāca anādinidhanāv etāv ubhāv eva mahāmune amūrtimantāv acalāv aprakampyau ca nirvraṇau
english: Janaka said: Both of these, O great sage, are without beginning or end, formless, unmoving, unshakable, and without flaw.

sanskrit: agrāhyāv ṛṣiśārdūla katham eko hy acetanaḥ cetanāvāṃs tathā caikaḥ kṣetrajña iti bhāṣitaḥ
english: Both are imperceptible, O tiger among sages — how then is the one said to be without consciousness, while the other, possessed of consciousness, is called the Knower of the Field?

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi viprendra kārtsnyena mokṣadharmam upāsase sākalyaṃ mokṣadharmasya śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: For you, O chief of brāhmaṇas, cultivate the doctrine of liberation in its entirety; I wish to hear, in truth, the whole of the law of liberation.

sanskrit: astitvaṃ kevalatvaṃ ca vinābhāvaṃ tathaiva ca tathaivotkramaṇasthānaṃ dehino 'pi viyujyataḥ
english: Its existence, its solitary state, and likewise its separateness — and also the station of departure for the embodied soul when it is loosed from the body.

sanskrit: kālena yad dhi prāpnoti sthānaṃ tad brūhi me dvija sāṃkhyajñānaṃ ca tattvena pṛthag yogaṃ tathaiva ca
english: Tell me, O twice-born, what station it reaches in due time, and the knowledge of Sāṃkhya in its essence, and Yoga as well, each apart.

sanskrit: ariṣṭāni ca tattvena vaktum arhasi sattama viditaṃ sarvam etat te pāṇāv āmalakaṃ yathā
english: And you ought to declare, in truth, the omens of death, O best of men; for all this is known to you as clearly as an āmalaka fruit upon the palm.

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca na śakyo nirguṇas tāta guṇīkartuṃ viśāṃ pate guṇavāṃś cāpy aguṇavān yathātattvaṃ nibodha me
english: Yājñavalkya said: The qualityless one cannot be made to possess qualities, my friend, O lord of peoples; and how the qualified one is also unqualified — learn that from me as it truly is.

sanskrit: guṇair hi guṇavān eva nirguṇaś cāguṇas tathā prāhur evaṃ mahātmāno munayas tattvadarśinaḥ
english: For it is by reason of the qualities that one is called qualified, and the qualityless one is without qualities — thus have the great-souled sages, the seers of truth, declared.

sanskrit: guṇasvabhāvas tv avyakto guṇān evābhivartate upayuṅkte ca tān eva sa caivājñaḥ svabhāvataḥ
english: The Unmanifest, whose nature is the qualities, abides amid the very qualities and makes use of those same qualities; and by its very nature it is unknowing.

sanskrit: avyaktas tu na jānīte puruṣo jñaḥ svabhāvataḥ na mattaḥ param astīti nityam evābhimanyate
english: The Unmanifest does not know, while the Spirit by its very nature is the knower; yet it forever imagines, 'There is nothing higher than I.'

sanskrit: anena kāraṇenaitad avyaktaṃ syād acetanam nityatvād akṣaratvāc ca kṣarāṇāṃ tattvato 'nyathā
english: For this reason the Unmanifest must be without consciousness; and by its eternity and imperishability it is, in truth, otherwise than the perishable things.

sanskrit: yadājñānena kurvīta guṇasargaṃ punaḥ punaḥ yadātmānaṃ na jānīte tadāvyaktam ihocyate
english: When, through unknowing, it brings forth the creation of the qualities again and again, and when it does not know itself, then it is here called the Unmanifest.

sanskrit: kartṛtvāc cāpi tattvānāṃ tattvadharmī tathocyate kartṛtvāc caiva yonīnāṃ yonidharmā tathocyate
english: Because it is the maker of the elemental principles, it is called the bearer of the nature of those principles; and because it is the maker of the wombs, it is called the bearer of the nature of the womb.

sanskrit: kartṛtvāt prakṛtīnāṃ tu tathā prakṛtidharmitā kartṛtvāc cāpi bījānāṃ bījadharmī tathocyate
english: Because it is the maker of the primal natures, it bears the nature of primal Nature; and because it is the maker of seeds, it is called the bearer of the nature of the seed.

sanskrit: guṇānāṃ prasavatvāc ca tathā prasavadharmavān kartṛtvāt pralayānāṃ ca tathā pralayadharmitā
english: And because it gives birth to the qualities, it bears the nature of bringing-forth; and because it is the maker of dissolutions, it bears the nature of dissolution.

sanskrit: bījatvāt prakṛtitvāc ca pralayatvāt tathaiva ca upekṣakatvād anyatvād abhimānāc ca kevalam
english: By its being seed, by its being Nature, and by its being dissolution as well, by its indifference, its otherness, and its self-conceit — it is the Sole.

sanskrit: manyante yatayaḥ śuddhā adhyātmavigatajvarāḥ anityaṃ nityam avyaktam evam etad dhi śuśruma
english: The pure ascetics, whose fever is gone through the science of the Self, deem the Unmanifest now transient, now eternal — thus indeed have we heard.

sanskrit: avyaktaikatvam ity āhur nānātvaṃ puruṣas tathā sarvabhūtadayāvantaḥ kevalaṃ jñānam āsthitāḥ
english: They declare the Unmanifest to be a oneness, and the Spirit likewise to be a manyness — those who, full of compassion for all beings, abide in pure knowledge alone.

sanskrit: anyaḥ sa puruṣo 'vyaktas tv adhruvo dhruvasaṃjñakaḥ yathā muñja iṣīkāyās tathaivaitad dhi jāyate
english: The Spirit is one thing, and the Unmanifest another — the latter unsteady yet bearing the name of steady; for just as the muñja reed is drawn from its inner stalk, so does this come to be.

sanskrit: anyaṃ ca maśakaṃ vidyād anyac codumbaraṃ tathā na codumbarasaṃyogair maśakas tatra lipyate
english: One should know the gnat to be one thing and the fig-tree another; the gnat is not stained there by its contact with the fig.

sanskrit: anya eva tathā matsyas tathānyad udakaṃ smṛtam na codakasya sparśena matsyo lipyati sarvaśaḥ
english: Likewise the fish is one thing, and the water is held to be another; and the fish is in no way stained by the touch of the water.

sanskrit: anyo hy agnir ukhāpy anyā nityam evam avaihi bhoḥ na copalipyate so 'gnir ukhāsaṃsparśanena vai
english: For the fire is one thing and the cauldron another — know it ever thus, good sir; and that fire is not defiled by its contact with the cauldron.

sanskrit: puṣkaraṃ tv anyad evātra tathānyad udakaṃ smṛtam na codakasya sparśena lipyate tatra puṣkaram
english: And here the lotus-leaf is one thing, while the water is held to be another; the lotus-leaf is not stained there by the touch of the water.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ saha saṃvāsaṃ vivāsaṃ caiva nityaśaḥ yathā tathainaṃ paśyanti na nityaṃ prākṛtā janāḥ
english: The dwelling-together and the parting of these pairs are perpetual; but common folk do not always see it as it truly is.

sanskrit: ye tv anyathaiva paśyanti na samyak teṣu darśanam te vyaktaṃ nirayaṃ ghoraṃ praviśanti punaḥ punaḥ
english: But those who see it otherwise have no right vision; they enter manifestly into dreadful hell, again and again.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyadarśanam etat te parisaṃkhyātam uttamam evaṃ hi parisaṃkhyāya sāṃkhyāḥ kevalatāṃ gatāḥ
english: This supreme vision of the Sāṃkhyas has been fully reckoned out for you; for having reckoned it thus, the Sāṃkhyas have attained to absolute solitude.

sanskrit: ye tv anye tattvakuśalās teṣām etan nidarśanam ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yogānām api darśanam
english: And for those others skilled in the principles, this is the teaching; hereafter I shall expound the vision of the Yogins as well.

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca sāṃkhyajñānaṃ mayā proktaṃ yogajñānaṃ nibodha me yathāśrutaṃ yathādṛṣṭaṃ tattvena nṛpasattama
english: Yājñavalkya said: The knowledge of Sāṃkhya has been declared by me; now learn from me the knowledge of Yoga, as heard and as seen, in its truth, O best of kings.

sanskrit: nāsti sāṃkhyasamaṃ jñānaṃ nāsti yogasamaṃ balam tāv ubhāv ekacaryau tu ubhāv anidhanau smṛtau
english: There is no knowledge equal to Sāṃkhya, no power equal to Yoga; both walk a single path, and both are held to be without end.

sanskrit: pṛthak pṛthak tu paśyanti ye 'lpabuddhiratā narāḥ vayaṃ tu rājan paśyāma ekam eva tu niścayāt
english: Men of little understanding see them as separate, each apart; but we, O king, with certainty see them as one and the same.

sanskrit: yad eva yogāḥ paśyanti tat sāṃkhyair api dṛśyate ekaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa tattvavit
english: That very thing which the Yogins behold is also seen by the followers of Sāṃkhya; he who sees Sāṃkhya and Yoga as one is the knower of truth.

sanskrit: rudrapradhānān aparān viddhi yogān paraṃtapa tenaiva cātha dehena vicaranti diśo daśa
english: Know the other Yogins to have Rudra as their chief, O scorcher of foes; and in that very body they roam through the ten directions.

sanskrit: yāvad dhi pralayas tāta sūkṣmeṇāṣṭaguṇena vai yogena lokān vicaran sukhaṃ saṃnyasya cānagha
english: Until the dissolution of the world, my friend, by means of the subtle eightfold Yoga he roams happily through the worlds, having renounced all, O sinless one.

sanskrit: vedeṣu cāṣṭaguṇitaṃ yogam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ sūkṣmam aṣṭaguṇaṃ prāhur netaraṃ nṛpasattama
english: In the Vedas, too, the wise call Yoga eightfold; they declare the subtle eightfold Yoga, and no other, O best of kings.

sanskrit: dviguṇaṃ yogakṛtyaṃ tu yogānāṃ prāhur uttamam saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ caiva yathāśāstranidarśanam
english: They declare the highest practice of the Yogins to be twofold — with qualities and without qualities — even as the scriptures teach.

sanskrit: dhāraṇā caiva manasaḥ prāṇāyāmaś ca pārthiva prāṇāyāmo hi saguṇo nirguṇaṃ dhāraṇaṃ manaḥ
english: There is the fixing of the mind and the restraint of the breath, O king: the restraint of breath is with quality, while the fixing of the mind is without quality.

sanskrit: yatra dṛśyeta muñcan vai prāṇān maithilasattama vātādhikyaṃ bhavaty eva tasmād dhi na samācaret
english: Where one would be seen letting go of the vital breaths, O best of the Maithilas, there an excess of wind arises; therefore one should not practise it so.

sanskrit: niśāyāḥ prathame yāme codanā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ madhye suptvā pare yāme dvādaśaiva tu codanāḥ
english: In the first watch of the night twelve exercises are enjoined; and having slept at midnight, in the last watch likewise twelve exercises.

sanskrit: tad evam upaśāntena dāntenaikāntaśīlinā ātmārāmeṇa buddhena yoktavyo ''tmā na saṃśayaḥ
english: Thus, by one grown calm, self-controlled, given to solitude, delighting in the Self, and awakened, the Self must be yoked — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: pañcānām indriyāṇāṃ tu doṣān ākṣipya pañcadhā śabdaṃ sparśaṃ tathā rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ tathaiva ca
english: Having cast off the fivefold faults of the five senses — sound, touch, and form, taste, and smell as well —

sanskrit: pratibhām apavargaṃ ca pratisaṃhṛtya maithila indriyagrāmam akhilaṃ manasy abhiniveśya ha
english: and having drawn back imagination and its surrender, O Maithila, having settled the whole host of the senses within the mind,

sanskrit: manas tathaivāhaṃkāre pratiṣṭhāpya narādhipa ahaṃkāraṃ tathā buddhau buddhiṃ ca prakṛtāv api
english: and having established the mind likewise in the I-sense, O lord of men, the I-sense in the intellect, and the intellect too in primal Nature,

sanskrit: evaṃ hi parisaṃkhyāya tato dhyāyeta kevalam virajaskamalaṃ nityam anantaṃ śuddham avraṇam
english: having thus reckoned it out, one should then meditate upon the Sole alone — stainless and spotless, eternal, infinite, pure, and without flaw,

sanskrit: tasthuṣaṃ puruṣaṃ sattvam abhedyam ajarāmaram śāśvataṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva īśānaṃ brahma cāvyayam
english: the abiding Spirit, the Real, indivisible, free from age and death, everlasting and imperishable, the Lord, the unfailing brahman.

sanskrit: yuktasya tu mahārāja lakṣaṇāny upadhārayet lakṣaṇaṃ tu prasādasya yathā tṛptaḥ sukhaṃ svapet
english: One should mark the signs of the man who is yoked, O great king: the mark of his serenity is that, like one who is sated, he sleeps in ease.

sanskrit: nivāte tu yathā dīpo jvalet snehasamanvitaḥ niścalordhvaśikhas tadvad yuktam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: As a lamp fed with oil burns in a windless place, its flame steady and upright, so the wise describe the man who is yoked.

sanskrit: pāṣāṇa iva meghotthair yathā bindubhir āhataḥ nālaṃ cālayituṃ śakyas tathā yuktasya lakṣaṇam
english: As a stone struck by the raindrops born of the clouds cannot be made to stir, such is the mark of the man who is yoked.

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣair vividhair gītavāditaiḥ kriyamāṇair na kampeta yuktasyaitan nidarśanam
english: By the blare of conch and kettledrum, by manifold songs and instruments being played, he would not be shaken — this is the token of the man who is yoked.

sanskrit: tailapātraṃ yathā pūrṇaṃ karābhyāṃ gṛhya pūruṣaḥ sopānam āruhed bhītas tarjyamāno 'sipāṇibhiḥ
english: As a man, grasping a brimful vessel of oil in both his hands, would mount a stairway, fearful, threatened by men with swords in hand,

sanskrit: saṃyatātmā bhayāt teṣāṃ na pātrād bindum utsṛjet tathaivottaramāṇasya ekāgramanasas tathā
english: and, his self controlled, would not for fear of them spill a drop from the vessel — even so is it with one who is ascending, his mind made single-pointed.

sanskrit: sthiratvād indriyāṇāṃ tu niścalatvāt tathaiva ca evaṃ yuktasya tu muner lakṣaṇāny upadhārayet
english: By the steadiness of his senses and likewise by their stillness, one should thus mark the signs of the sage who is yoked.

sanskrit: sa yuktaḥ paśyati brahma yat tat paramam avyayam mahatas tamaso madhye sthitaṃ jvalanasaṃnibham
english: That yoked one beholds the brahman, which is supreme and imperishable, set in the midst of the great darkness, blazing like fire.

sanskrit: etena kevalaṃ yāti tyaktvā deham asākṣikam kālena mahatā rājañ śrutir eṣā sanātanī
english: By this he attains the Absolute, having cast aside the unwitnessed body, after a great length of time, O king — this is the eternal revelation.

sanskrit: etad dhi yogaṃ yogānāṃ kim anyad yogalakṣaṇam vijñāya tad dhi manyante kṛtakṛtyā manīṣiṇaḥ
english: This indeed is the Yoga of the Yogins — what other mark of Yoga could there be? Having known it, the wise hold themselves to have done all that is to be done.

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca tathaivotkramamāṇaṃ tu śṛṇuṣvāvahito nṛpa padbhyām utkramamāṇasya vaiṣṇavaṃ sthānam ucyate
english: Yājñavalkya said: Hear now attentively of the soul's departing, O king. For one departing through the feet, the station of Viṣṇu is declared.

sanskrit: jaṅghābhyāṃ tu vasūn devān āpnuyād iti naḥ śrutam jānubhyāṃ ca mahābhāgān devān sādhyān avāpnuyāt
english: Through the shanks he would attain the Vasu gods — so have we heard — and through the knees he would reach the greatly blessed Sādhya gods.

sanskrit: pāyunotkramamāṇas tu maitraṃ sthānam avāpnuyāt pṛthivīṃ jaghanenātha ūrubhyāṃ tu prajāpatim
english: Departing through the fundament, he would attain the station of Mitra; through the hips, the Earth; and through the thighs, Prajāpati.

sanskrit: pārśvābhyāṃ maruto devān nāsābhyām indum eva ca bāhubhyām indram ity āhur urasā rudram eva ca
english: Through the two flanks the Marut gods, and through the nostrils the Moon; through the arms, they say, Indra; and through the breast, Rudra.

sanskrit: grīvāyās tam ṛṣiśreṣṭhaṃ naram āpnoty anuttamam viśvedevān mukhenātha diśaḥ śrotreṇa cāpnuyāt
english: Through the neck he attains that best of seers, the unsurpassed Nara; through the mouth, the All-Gods; and through the ear, the quarters of space.

sanskrit: ghrāṇena gandhavahanaṃ netrābhyāṃ sūryam eva ca bhrūbhyāṃ caivāśvinau devau lalāṭena pitṝn atha
english: Through the sense of smell, the bearer of fragrance, the Wind; through the eyes, Sūrya; through the brows, the two Aśvin gods; and through the forehead, the Fathers.

sanskrit: brahmāṇam āpnoti vibhuṃ mūrdhnā devāgrajaṃ tathā etāny utkramaṇasthānāny uktāni mithileśvara
english: Through the crown of the head he attains the all-pervading Brahmā, foremost of the gods. These are the stations of departure, O lord of Mithilā.

sanskrit: ariṣṭāni tu vakṣyāmi vihitāni manīṣibhiḥ saṃvatsaraviyogasya saṃbhaveyuḥ śarīriṇaḥ
english: Now I shall declare the omens of death, set forth by the wise, which would arise in an embodied one a year before his parting.

sanskrit: yo 'rundhatīṃ na paśyeta dṛṣṭapūrvāṃ kadā cana tathaiva dhruvam ity āhuḥ pūrṇenduṃ dīpam eva ca khaṇḍābhāsaṃ dakṣiṇatas te 'pi saṃvatsarāyuṣaḥ
english: He who can no longer see Arundhatī, though he has seen her before, and likewise the Pole-star, the full moon, and a lamp — or who sees them broken in appearance on the right — such men too have but a year to live.

sanskrit: paracakṣuṣi cātmānaṃ ye na paśyanti pārthiva ātmacchāyākṛtībhūtaṃ te 'pi saṃvatsarāyuṣaḥ
english: And those who do not see themselves in another's eye, formed as the image of their own shadow, O king — they too have but a year to live.

sanskrit: atidyutir atiprajñā aprajñā cādyutis tathā prakṛter vikriyāpattiḥ ṣaṇmāsān mṛtyulakṣaṇam
english: Excess of splendor, excess of insight, loss of insight, and loss of splendor — this change-and-disorder of one's nature is a sign of death within six months.

sanskrit: daivatāny avajānāti brāhmaṇaiś ca virudhyate kṛṣṇaśyāvacchavicchāyaḥ ṣaṇmāsān mṛtyulakṣaṇam
english: He who scorns the gods and quarrels with the brāhmaṇas, whose hue grows dark, dusky, and corpse-like — that is a sign of death within six months.

sanskrit: śīrṇanābhi yathā cakraṃ chidraṃ somaṃ prapaśyati tathaiva ca sahasrāṃśuṃ saptarātreṇa mṛtyubhāk
english: He who sees the moon pierced like a wheel with a worn-out nave, and likewise the thousand-rayed sun, is doomed to die within seven nights.

sanskrit: śavagandham upāghrāti surabhiṃ prāpya yo naraḥ devatāyatanasthas tu ṣaḍrātreṇa sa mṛtyubhāk
english: The man who smells the stench of a corpse though a sweet fragrance is at hand, while standing in the temple of a god, is doomed to die within six nights.

sanskrit: karṇanāsāvanamanaṃ dantadṛṣṭivirāgitā saṃjñālopo nirūṣmatvaṃ sadyomṛtyunidarśanam
english: A drooping of the ears and nose, a fading of the teeth and the sight, a loss of awareness, and a lack of warmth — these are tokens of immediate death.

sanskrit: akasmāc ca sravedyasya vāmam akṣi narādhipa mūrdhataś cotpated dhūmaḥ sadyomṛtyunidarśanam
english: And he whose left eye streams without cause, O lord of men, and from whose head smoke seems to rise — these are tokens of immediate death.

sanskrit: etāvanti tv ariṣṭāni viditvā mānavo ''tmavān niśi cāhani cātmānaṃ yojayet paramātmani
english: Having known these many omens, the self-possessed man should, by night and by day, yoke his own self to the Supreme Self.

sanskrit: pratīkṣamāṇas tat kālaṃ yat kālaṃ prati tad bhavet athāsya neṣṭaṃ maraṇaṃ sthātum icched imāṃ kriyām
english: Awaiting that hour, whatever the hour against which it is to come — but if death is not desired by him and he wishes to remain, let him perform this practice.

sanskrit: sarvagandhān rasāṃś caiva dhārayeta samāhitaḥ tathā hi mṛtyuṃ jayati tatpareṇāntarātmanā
english: Composed, let him hold fast all scents and tastes; for in this way, with the inmost self intent upon That, he conquers death.

sanskrit: sasāṃkhyadhāraṇaṃ caiva viditvā manujarṣabha jayec ca mṛtyuṃ yogena tatpareṇāntarātmanā
english: And having learned the practice of fixation together with Sāṃkhya, O bull among men, he may conquer death by Yoga, with the inmost self intent upon That.

sanskrit: gacchet prāpyākṣayaṃ kṛtsnam ajanma śivam avyayam śāśvataṃ sthānam acalaṃ duṣprāpam akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: He would attain and pass on to the imperishable Whole — unborn, blessed, and unfailing — the everlasting, unmoving station, hard to win for those whose selves are unperfected.

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca avyaktasthaṃ paraṃ yat tat pṛṣṭas te 'haṃ narādhipa paraṃ guhyam imaṃ praśnaṃ śṛṇuṣvāvahito nṛpa
english: Yājñavalkya said: That supreme thing seated in the Unmanifest, about which you have questioned me, O lord of men — hear attentively this most secret question, O king.
